README: Independent cross-check for web/src/skymap/frames/shared/sidereal.ts's
altAzToRaDec against skyfield (the astro core's own ephemeris library,
ssc/astro/ CLAUDE.md) -- sidereal.ts is a deliberate, separate TypeScript
reimplementation of GMST + the alt/az<->ra/dec spherical transform (see its
own module doc comment), which is exactly the kind of thing that can drift
unnoticed from the trusted Python model. This fixture pins it down.
Each row is: given a site, a UTC instant and a geometric (alt, az), what
topocentric apparent-of-date (RA, Dec) does skyfield report for that
direction. sidereal.ts's altAzToRaDec is expected to agree to within the
tolerance in sidereal.test.ts, dominated by the mean-vs-apparent sidereal
time gap (equation of the equinoxes, up to ~1s of time / ~15 arcsec of RA)
since sidereal.ts deliberately uses mean sidereal time, not apparent
(see its own doc comment) -- not a bug, but exactly why the tolerance is
arcminutes, not arcseconds.
Sites: Tromso (69.65N, inside the Arctic Circle), Fairbanks and Nome
(high north, negative and near-(-180) longitude), London (small negative
longitude), Sydney and Ushuaia (southern), Suva (near +180 longitude).
Instants: both solstices, the March equinox, both 2026 EU/US DST
transition dates, and 2026-09-08 (this task's 'today') -- a spread
across the year exercising the GMST polynomial's T/T^2/T^3 terms.
alt/az: alt=0 (horizon, all four cardinal azimuths), mid-altitude,
high-altitude, near-zenith (89.9 deg) and exactly the zenith (90 deg,
a documented singularity in both implementations -- azimuth is passed
through as 0 by convention in each).
Regenerate with skyfield 1.55 by re-running the
generator described in this file's own accompanying agent report
(no ephemeris kernel needed: from_altaz()/radec(epoch='date') use only
Earth orientation, not planetary positions).
